To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the binding of short Acr-linked oligonucleotide third strands to target DNA sequences containing adjacent purine and pyrimidine blocks is dependent on both metal ion and the nature of the target sequence.

(a) Acr-T5-G5 binds to the sequence G6T-G6.A6C-6, in the absence of any metal ion, to form a triplex with antiparallel G.GC triple helices, (b) the central guanine of this triplex is not recognized by Acr-T5- G5 and is accessible to dimethyl sulphate, (c) Acr-G5-T5 binds to the T6-G6.C6-A6 sequence
the acridine-linked third strands Acr-T5 G5 and Acr- G5T5 form intermolecular triplexes with the target sites G6 T6.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of oligonucleotide that is able to bind to DNA sequences containing adjacent purine and pyrimidine tracts.
the use of acridine-linked third strands to form intermolecular DNA triplexes, and has demonstrated the formation of triplexes at two adjacent sites in a DNA fragment.
the design and synthesis of oligonucleotidic third strands that can be used to form DNA triple helices in vitro.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the formation of interstrand DNA triplexes is highly sequence-dependent and that the binding of third strands is affected by the presence of bivalent metal ions, which may stabilize triplex structures with mismatches.

the formation of interstrand DNA triplexes can occur in the presence of divalent cations and at physiological pH, and that these triplexes are stabilized by the presence of purine-pyrimidine sequences.
the formation of triple helices is dependent on both the sequence and the composition of the oligonucleotide and the target DNA, and on the pH and the metal ions present.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Acr-TG and Acr-GT form triplexes with purine-pyrimidine-purine sequences in the presence of either magnesium or manganese, and that the latter ion facilitates the formation of triplexes containing mismatches.

, at pH 7 and in the presence of either magnesium chloride or manganese chloride, the third strands Acr-T5GC and Acr-GT5 form intermolecular triplexes with their complementary targets G6T6.C6A and C6A6.T6G6 respectively.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the formation of DNA triple helices can be studied using short acridinium-linked oligonucleotide probes, and that the formation of triplexes is dependent on the sequence of the target site, and the metal ion present in solution.
the formation of interstrand DNA triple helices is a highly sequence-specific process and is not limited to the formation of G.GC triple helices.

the formation of interstrand DNA triple helices can be facilitated by the presence of a divalent metal ion, such as manganese, which may be able to stabilize a triplex containing a single or double mismatch.
